newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain union says labour talks close to standstill.
newsitem.headline: Spain union says labour talks close to standstill.

text.p: Final negotiations between trade unions and employers on the reform of Spain's labour market have almost reached a standstill, a union leader said in an interview on Sunday.
"The negotiation process is in an enormously difficult situation, which is closer to disaccord than accord," Candido Mendez, Secretary General of the UGT trade union, told local agency Europa Press.
Spain wants trade unions and employers to agree measures to liberalise the labour market to help cut unemployment and prepare the economy for Europe's Monetary Union.
The government has said that if an agreement is not reached between the two parties by March, it is prepared to step in and resolve the issue.
Mendez said the two sides would try again to reconcile their differences in the coming week.

"It would be wrong to say that at no moment the process has been close to a deal...at the moment, the difficulties are clearly more evident, because we are in the final phases of conclusions," said Mendez.
Mendez said the two sides were still at odds on the degree of job stability and the nature of firing.
"We are talking about stability and quality of jobs while employers want to maintain the precariousness," he said.

"And while we think it is necessary to define a framework of cooperation to identify the causes of firing, employers want to strengthen their discretion," Mendez said. ((-- Madrid newsroom + 34 1 585 2161))
